chapter_title: Concerning Wisdom; it is far superior when on the Tongue than in the Heart of the Person.
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by a didactic analogy-teaching (child-in-womb/birth; fire-in-wood/light) with a dialogue wrapper. It lacks the hallmark “cosmos→cosmos” systematic architecture (named aeons, degree-lists, body/universe maps), so the extracted ‘core’ here is best understood as an older homiletic correspondential instruction embedded in a Kephalaia Q&A frame rather than a clear fragment of the deepest cosmological substrate. No NT citation overlay or institutional/pastoral graft is present; the primary late layer is the hagiographic dialogue frame (apostle/disciple, rejoicing/obeisance closure).

paragraphs.core_text: Behold, when a person will be taught wise wisdom in his heart, and he seals it in his doctrine, so shall you find him rejoicing greatly about it. However, [sh]all his [ ... ... ] to him, more th[an] when he may pro-c[laim ... ] and utter it. ⟨p.205⟩ He shall be enlightened by it, and [t]hat [wisdom] shall shine forth the more in him. It is un-veil[ed be]fore him, and through it he assumes power and truth.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/hagiographic frame formula and attribution (“Once again… disciple… before the apostle… He questioned him, saying: I entreat you, my master…”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening ‘Once again… disciple… apostle… I entreat you’ is Kephalaia frame; the remaining content states the teaching thesis (wisdom internal vs proclaimed) without institutional or NT markers.

paragraphs.core_text: I understand [ ... ] that this word I have uttered is correct. I know that the wis-dom I have been taught is spread through my heart and perfected in my soul. (However), it is not found like the splendour in me, so that I regard it [ad]vanced, except when I shall proclaim it by my mouth and utter it to others. Indeed, when I proclaim it, I am giving it to the ears [of] others to hear. Would I do these same things, even if I had never heard it in [my] days of being? Would I desire greatly and my heart be drawn to the wis-dom I now proclaim? [I entreat y]ou, my master, that you might instruct me as to [w/hy] this wisdom becomes more advanced when I proclaim it, than when it is sealed in my heart.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution (“That disciple speaks further before the apostle:”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The ‘apostle’ attribution is late frame; the remainder is a thematic, non-cosmological instruction/question continuing the wisdom-on-tongue vs wisdom-in-heart contrast.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] it is superior in my mouth when I proclaim it than when it is set in m[y heart]. You yourself rejoice in it; and the other one who hears it from you, he shall rejoice in it, and be enlightened [by] it and receive thereby permanent strength.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution and evaluative address (“Then the apostle speaks… Well [do] you ask! And great is this lesson…”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Clear hagiographic speaker-tag ‘apostle’ plus commendation formula; the extracted lines are the compact teaching claim about proclamation producing enlightenment/strength.

paragraphs.core_text: For like this matter, just so a small b[o]y who is conceived in the belly of his mother. He [ ... he] turns in his mother's womb, filling her womb. The mother knows and understands that this child she conceives is alive within her. She rejoices over him until [the tim]e when she gives birth. And he comes from her alive with his [limbs whole] and perfect in beauty, without defect, ⟨p.206⟩ [in] the living open air that is more sp[ac]ious than the first air he was in. He fills his eyes with the light and speaks with his living voice in the way of they who are born.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal analogical exposition with no dialogue tags, institutional terms, or citations; functions as the first correspondential paradigm (hidden life → manifest birth).

paragraphs.core_text: Now, the time when this woman conceives the child in her belly, her joy at conceiving him in her womb is not so [ve]ry great as when she gives birth and sees him; and is full of his [be]auty and stature in the space of a single moment. The love and joy over him shall be a hundred [t]imes greater than it was, now that she has given birth and seen him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of the child paradigm in an expository voice; despite a slight ‘affect’ register, it stays within the analogy rather than exhorting an audience or naming institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: For the first time when she conceived him in her belly, his beauty and the sight of his eyes was hidden from his m[o/th]er; but when she gave birth to him she saw his beauty. His s[t]ature and his loveliness came before the e[ye]s of his f[athe]r [a]nd his mother and all his relatives. They shall rejoic[e] over him more and more when they look upon him face to face and see his beauty and delightfulness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the ‘hidden → seen’ logic of the paradigm; no frame formulas or later application markers intrude.

paragraphs.core_text: Just as in this simile, the wisdom that is present [in] the heart of the person is like the living child who is co[nceived] in the belly of his mother. And when he is taught and seals it in his heart, it becomes like the child who shall be born, and they see his beauty.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explicit correspondence application (wisdom-in-heart ↔ child-in-womb/birth) stated as a mapping; still not institutional/NT and remains within the analogical system.

paragraphs.core_text: So, in this way, the wisdom that the person proclaims, speak[ng] it from his heart, shall be advanced more and mor[e]. Its en-hancement and glory shall double from the time when the bea-uty and splendour of the saying will be displayed before the eyes [of t]hey who hear it, and it shall also advance for you [ ... ... ] your hearing, and you are astonished at what you proclai[m].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Expository ‘how it works’ voice (increase/doubling, display before eyes/ears) with no hagiographic tags; slight second-person residue does not pivot into institutional exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, the wisdom is like this, while it is hidden in the heart of the person. [Bef]ore he has uttered it, it is just like [the blaze] of fire that is hidden in wood. An[d] that wood is [set aflame] by the blaze of the fire, but the garment of fir[e that exists in] the wood is not apparent. Indeed, you can see [ ... ] ⟨p.207⟩ wood and they put them in a single house. It is impossible to [put li]ght to that house as long as the light within [ ... ] until the time when they are added to the fire, and the light [comes f]orth from them. It is possible for that entire house [to be] lit by the light of a single piece of wood.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second paradigm (fire-in-wood) articulated as a process-mechanism (hidden light → manifest light) without dialogue frame; ‘Once again’ here functions as internal rhetorical iteration, not Kephalaia speaker-tagging.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case with the wisdom that is in the heart of the person. [It] is like the fire that is hidden in the wood, as its light is not [d]isplayed. For its part, the wisdom is like this: its li[ght] is hidden and its glory is hidden in the heart; but when the person will proclaim it, its glory shall be displayed before the eyes and the ears of a multitude.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Tight mapping statement (wisdom ↔ hidden fire/light) in impersonal explanatory style; no institutional vocabulary or citations.

paragraphs.core_text: So, if the wisdom is like the paradigms you have taught me, why are there some people who shall hear the word of wisdom and rejoice in it and give glory to it; when others shall listen to it and neither rejoice [i]n it nor receive glory amongst them?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution (“Once again, for a second time this disciple speaks to the apostle:”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Speaker-tag ‘disciple… apostle’ is frame; the remaining sentence is a substantive problem-question extending the teaching (differential reception) without pastoral regulation.
Pure dialogue management (‘the apostle speaks… I will persuade you… teach you’) with no independent teaching content.

paragraphs.core_text: For in this respect the wisdom is like this child about whom I have told you, the one who [was] born from the woman. Now, when he will be born, his father and mother and family circle shall rejoice over him. However, you find others grieving by reason of him, [s]ince they are strangers to him. These are not reckoned among his family. [They do n]ot rejoice over him, because he is not of their race.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Analogy extended to a second dimension (kin vs strangers) in an explanatory voice; no institutional naming (church/elect) or citation formulas.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also [the case] with the wisdom. When it is proclaimed by the mouth of the teacher, these who are [a]kin to it shall receive it to them and rejoice in it; but [those] who are strangers to it neither rejoice in it [ ... ] nor receive it to them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Direct mapping from the ‘kin/strangers’ paradigm to wisdom-reception; ‘teacher’ remains generic and not an institutional office-list, so the mapping does not cross into pastoral regulation.

paragraphs.core_text: Just like the light of [the fire, which I] proclaim[ed] to you, that shall come from the wood [and be apparent o]utside before the eyes of every one. ⟨p.208⟩ So, [wh]oever looks shall see the light that has [come fro]m the wood; but whoever is blind does not see the [fir]e.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Paradigm reiterated (visibility vs blindness) as a natural correspondence; still not anchored to contemporary polemic or institutional categories.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case with the wisdom, when it will be pro-claimed. The person, in whom is the [Mi]nd, of him is the wisdom. Whenever he may hear it, he shall receive it in to him; but the one who has no Mind in him is a stranger to it. He neither receives it in to him, nor shall he listen to [it].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Introduces Manichaean technical term Mind as an inner capacity determining receptivity; remains doctrinal/explanatory rather than exhortative or institutional, suggesting a teaching layer rather than later pastoral graft.
Formulaic closure reaction (rejoiced, persuaded, obeisance, sat down) characteristic of Kephalaia hagiographic framing.
